title: Black Hole Recordings New Releases – Week 42
excerpt: Find the latest electronic music news, features, interviews, videos and podcasts from Beatportal - the reference for DJs and dance music artists.
content:
A selection of this week’s standout releases across the dancefloor.

From timeless appeal of trance to the more exploratory side of melodic techno and progressive house, this week’s releases cover plenty of ground. Heartfelt vocals, unexpected ideas, and evolving grooves bring a mix of emotion and energy, with each artist putting their own spin on the music.

KEY4050 – Stay In Your Lane [Black Hole Recordings]

KEY4050 return with “Stay In Your Lane,” the title track and third release from their upcoming album. This tech trance cut reflects John O’Callaghan and Bryan Kearney’s experience after more than 20 years behind the decks, exploring different styles before finding their way back to what feels most natural. The record carries that same mindset: staying true to their musical identity without giving up the urge to experiment.

Following their debut album, Tales From The Temple, this new one marks another chapter for the duo, shaped by years of exploring what trance can be while knowing exactly where their strengths lie. With “Stay In Your Lane,” KEY4050 make that philosophy clear: evolution doesn’t mean leaving your roots behind.

Ciaran McAuley & Liel Kolet – Something To Hold [Black Hole Recordings]

Ciaran McAuley and Liel Kolet join forces on “Something To Hold,” a vocal trance release built around Liel’s angelic voice and a heartfelt love song that began in a writing session with Sarah de Warren in Los Angeles. A beautiful chord progression quickly inspired them to write something powerful, and within just a few hours, they felt they had created a ballad that could connect with people on a deeper level.

Ciaran McAuley later took the song under his wing, understanding the original vision and bringing it to life through his production. Liel says she still feels uplifted and moved every time she hears the finished version, and that personal connection comes through in a song shaped by the emotions of the people who created it.

EGGSTA & That Girl – The Kick [Black Hole Recordings]

EGGSTA and That Girl take a different approach with “The Kick,” a melodic techno cut that plays with the way a record comes together. Spoken vocals introduce each musical element one by one, gradually building tension until everything leads to the defining moment: the kick hitting in the drop.

As their first experimental collaboration, the project takes both artists into new territory, bringing their creative styles into a more techy, progressive direction. The vocal concept gives “The Kick” its own character, turning the process of building a record into the main attraction.

We had so much fun creating this record and pushing ourselves to explore new sounds and blend different genres into something completely unexpected for both of our audiences.

- EGGSTA & That Girl

LTN pres. Ghostbeat & MIDI Kittyy – Ecstasy [Magik Muzik]

LTN pres. Ghostbeat and MIDI Kittyy take a more patient approach on “Ecstasy,” letting a steady progressive groove and MIDI Kittyy’s tender vocals set the mood. Her voice floats above the arrangement, while the melodies slowly open up, giving the music a warmth that feels almost like being wrapped in a familiar embrace.

The second single from LTN’s upcoming album Into The Storm, “Ecstasy” captures that moment when you get so lost in the music that the outside world no longer matters. Instead of chasing a big drop, it lets the vocals and melodies carry the emotion, creating an atmosphere that feels intimate, soothing, and quietly captivating.

Harmonee – Promise Me (Figtronica Remix) [Gameroom Records]

Harmonee’s “Promise Me” gets a new twist with Figtronica’s remix, turning a song about the excitement and uncertainty of a new relationship into something more energetic and danceable. While the original asks someone to stay, the remix shifts the story to the point where two people have grown closer, and the thought of losing what they’ve found becomes harder to imagine.

That change comes through in the arrangement, with bolder synths and a stronger dance groove balancing the darker, more melancholic undertones. Romantic and uplifting, yet with a hint of tension, Figtronica’s version captures that stage of a relationship when the initial hesitation fades and being together starts to feel natural.
